families.note: a knife held in one hand, edge forward: a diagonal cut from the right shoulder and a straight thrust, one after the other (spec 015 R3, 'golpe curto (faca)')
a short heavy tool or blade in one hand (machete, hatchet, hammer, baton, skillet): chopped down from over the right shoulder, the body turning into it as in the knife's cut

a club in both hands (bat, pipe, crowbar, sledgehammer): drawn back behind the right shoulder, swung level through the chest with the hips and shoulders turning, and carried round over the left shoulder (follow-through)
a long weapon in both hands with its weight at the head or an edge (axe, pickaxe, katana): swung flat and low from the right shoulder across the body, the hips leading, as the shovel's swing
